subsystem: Collection: registry, native feeds, Jev, Apify (key: collection)
summary: The collection stage is well guarded (DNS-pinned HTTPS, 1 MB bodies, 8/20/25 s deadlines, $0.25 reservation ledger, 133 passing unit tests in 1.8 s) but starves the stages after it. Measured live through the production adapter on 22 Oct: 80% of the 378 items the 32 free feeds return carry under 400 characters of text, the five daily feeds median 94-168 characters and Hacker News is 80% empty, so briefs fall below the 400-character single-image rule and the model writes from a sentence. The article page is fetched twice (HTML enrichment and the media step) and its text discarded both times. The prompt-injection regex drops ordinary AI vocabulary ('tool call', 'system prompt'): today it removed the vLLM 0.30-0.32 and Ollama 0.40.7 release notes, a Simon Willison tool post and a Register story. 70% of night-1 candidates were held and nothing in TypeScript, SQL or the UI can release or re-review a held row (the Jev save path skips non-new rows). Registry weights are set in registry.json and read nowhere; a hard-coded tier table in dneskai-events.ts does the job instead. There are zero Czech or regional sources and eight of the 32 feeds are BoardlessAI marketing-stage sources. Apify (off) is the only multi-image supply and would cost cents a night, but two latent faults must be fixed before switching it on: one failed paid start writes a null cost that blocks Jev on every later night with no resolution path, and the reservation-based $0.25 cap has $0.002 of headroom on Sundays, so widening Instagram makes the whole run end 'held' before Jev. Docs disagree with code on source deadlines, on which adapters run, and on what the one Apify test cost.

facts.fact: Jev call: model 'jev-1.13.0' at POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone, price $0.042 per million input tokens (output free), 8 candidates per call, at most 16 calls per run (ceil(pending/8)), history <= 148 records (store supplies <= 20: 7 selected + 6 published + 7 approved), each candidate sent as title <= 120 and text <= 600 UTF-16 units, history as 40 + 64; request <= 60,000 bytes and state <= 28,000 bytes checked before the reservation. Three questions per candidate: category choice over ai-news/tech-news/marketing/tool/ai-project/other, relevance (noul), duplicate choice over history and earlier batch items. Decision: held if in-scope probability (1 - P(other)) < 0.9, or duplicate confidence < 0.8 or P(choice) < 0.9 or choice 'uncertain', or relevance < 0.85; rejected if relevance <= 0.15 and P(other) >= 0.9, or category 'other' with everything certain; duplicate if a history/batch record is chosen; otherwise 'new' (eligible). Cost = input_tokens * 0.042 / 1e6.

facts.fact: Candidate states are new | held | duplicate | rejected | selected ('unselected' in the brief = classified 'new' rows that the finish function did not pick). Held reasons: collection-review-{category|duplicate|relevance} (Jev uncertainty), collection-editorial-out-of-scope is rejected not held, collection-cost-unverified (Jev stage not ok / cost unknown), collection-empty-source-text (no title and no text at creation), insert-time hold when publishedAt is null or text empty, collection-source-date-unavailable-or-stale (finish: news older than 48 h, others older than 30 days). No code path releases or re-reviews a held candidate: the pending filter takes only status 'new' with category null, the Jev save RPC skips any row whose status is not 'new', the finish function reads only 'new'/'duplicate'/'selected', the API routes for candidates are GET-only (collect POST is the tick), and the Sources tab renders held as a badge.

facts.fact: Money guard: every paid stage reserves before the call under an advisory lock ($0.04 Instagram, $0.003 Jev); the sum of reservations (not measured costs) across the owner's stages for the Prague day must stay <= $0.25, and Instagram items <= 50/day; the day is re-checked after the reservation and before the provider call; a reservation whose cost is null or above the reservation anywhere in the owner's history (no run/date filter) makes every later paid claim raise 'collection cost unresolved', the runner holds Instagram stages (collection-cost-unresolved), holds Jev stages, and the finish function skips selection while a run carries an unknown cost; a claim exception finishes the whole run 'held' (collection-paid-admission-blocked).

findings.title: The feed provider defaults to the retired bridge and carries dormant bridge and preview plumbing
findings.claim: Unset or 'bridge' sends signed requests to Quorum's /admin/api/marketing-collection, which has answered 503 since 21 October; .env.example ships 'bridge'; the blockers list reports collection-bridge-unconfigured in any non-native environment; the provider keeps the preview-share fetcher and three MARKETING_DNESKAI_SOURCE_* variables among 24 switches.

evidence.excerpt: The code default stays `bridge`. Rollback: set `MARKETING_DNESKAI_FEED_PROVIDER=bridge` (or unset it) and redeploy.

impact.reason: Removing the dead bridge default removes a misconfiguration trap; wait for the owner to close the rollback window.

findings.recommendation: Once the owner closes the rollback window: default to native, delete the bridge branch, the preview-share fetcher and the MARKETING_DNESKAI_SOURCE_* variables, keep the dneskai-feed/1 envelope as the internal contract, and remove the bridge blocker. This is one step of the consolidation decision (owner goal 7).

truth.evidence: .env.example:148 ships bridge; dneskai-providers.ts:42-48 keeps the bridge signer and preview-share fetcher; dneskai-store.ts:87 reports collection-bridge-unconfigured unless the provider is native; native-feeds.md:171 says the code default stays bridge. The production value (native per the doc) was not read (Vercel env not inspected).

findings.impactStatement: Simplicity/risk: a new environment built from the example routes collection to a dead endpoint; every reader must understand two providers and 24 switches. Owner minutes: setup and debugging.

findings.title: Instagram candidates repeat the caption as title and caption-less carousels are held forever
findings.claim: An Instagram candidate's title is the first 500 characters of its caption and its text the full caption, so Jev reads the same opening twice (120 + 600 units). A post with no caption has no title and no text and is created 'held' with collection-empty-source-text, although an image-only carousel from a daily profile is the strongest picture supply the pipeline has.

impact.reason: Matters only once Apify is on; small change.

findings.recommendation: Use the caption's first sentence as the title and the remainder as text; keep caption-less posts with >= 2 images as 'new' with an imageOnly flag so they can join an event as supporting media without ever being quoted.

truth.evidence: dneskai-providers.ts:121 passes the first 500 characters of the caption as title and the caption as text; :81 creates a row held when title and text are empty; :135 sends Jev title 120 + text 600.

findings.impactStatement: Quality: wasted Jev context and lost carousels. Dollars: negligible.
